subject: MedScale — interactive session livelock / SLA impact
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medscale.com>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: jin.park@medscale.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: interactive sessions — sudden client timeouts and reconnect storms

Monica / Redwood team,

We started seeing a big problem at ~15:20 PST today: a subset of our interactive users experience repeated streaming timeouts and immediate client reconnects. On our side the client shows an "idle stream disconnect" after ~8–12s even when tokens are actively being produced. This is driving a sharp spike in 429/5xx on our telemetry and is causing session livelock where the client keeps retrying until the UI becomes unusable.

A few datapoints:
- Affected region: us-west-2 (primarily)
- Model endpoint: redwood/gptx-13b:v2 (we were on latest pinned variant)
- Sample request ids: 1a2f-3b4c-5d6e, 1a2f-3b4c-5d70, 1a2f-3b4c-5d71 (attached list)
- Observed client-side idle disconnects: 8–12s after last token
- Our backend recorded increased 429 responses and occasional 503s, correlated with repeated reconnect bursts

This is impacting a production cohort (MedScale Pro) — several customers reported degraded workflows and one customer triaged to procurement asking for SLA credits. Can you confirm whether there was a rollout/infra change? We need an initial mitigation plan ASAP — if needed we can roll traffic back to previous model variant.

I've attached logs and a small reqid list. Please escalate to engineering / SRE.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Integrations, MedScale

Attachments: medscale-logs-20270329.zip (log bundle), medscale-session-sample-reqids.txt (plain text)
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medscale.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: interactive sessions — sudden client timeouts and reconnect storms

Liam — thanks for the quick heads up and for attaching the logs. We're pulling the traces now. Initial triage questions while SRE looks at the traces:

- Were you using streaming with client keepalive? If so, what keepalive interval is set on the client?
- Did you observe any large spike in concurrent sessions from a specific org id or API key?
- Can you share a single full request/response pair for one of the sample reqids (we only need the headers + timing windows)

I have looped in Hannah (ops lead) and Sean (SRE lead) — we'll treat this as an elevated incident until we have a confirmed root cause.

Action items we are starting immediately:
- SRE to correlate 429/5xx spikes with host-level and queue metrics
- Engineering to verify recent rollout and kernel/quant changes for gptx-13b:v2
- If verified, propose target mitigations (traffic cap, rollback to v1, temporary routing to dedicated pool)

We will follow up in 30–45 mins with a short update.

— Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medscale.com>, Jin Park <jin.park@medscale.com>, procurement@medscale.com
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: MedScale — exec escalation + immediate mitigations (traffic cap & model rollback option)

Team — escalating this to ops and exec attention. Summary:
- Impact: elevated 429/5xx from repeated client reconnects causing "livelock" in streaming sessions for MedScale Pro customers (us-west-2)
- Timeline: began 2027-03-29 ~15:20 PST
- Evidence: customer logs + attached reqid list; HubSpot ticket linked below

Immediate mitigations I am initiating now (please action):
1) Traffic cap: route at most 20% of MedScale traffic to redwood/gptx-13b:v2; remaining traffic route to gptx-13b:v1 (fallback variant) — Sean, please implement traffic steering and confirm rollback window.
2) Keepalive/idle: increase streaming keepalive to 45s on the platform-side default and add temporary client-side advisory to MedScale docs to set keepalive=40s (Monica to coordinate).
3) KV cache: flush any stale prefix caches that might be causing session fragmentation (Jonas to coordinate with runtime team).
4) Telemetry: enable higher-sampling traces for the affected endpoint and surface token-level latencies to the support dashboard.

SLA/credits: Liam, we hear your ask about SLA credits. We will collect impact metrics and route to finance + legal. I will draft a credit memo if mitigation does not resolve the issue within the next 24 hours.

Decision request (need by 10:00 AM PST): If rolling back to gptx-13b:v1 is acceptable to the business for short-term stability, we should do it now. If MedScale requests no rollback, we'll continue with caps + keepalive adjustments and monitor.

I've opened INF-4217 in the internal tracker and linked the HubSpot deal so SRE/Eng/Account teams can coordinate on a single timeline. Please reply all with confirmations as you act.

— Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: (internal runbook reference: INF-4217)

To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medscale.com>, Jin Park <jin.park@medscale.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedScale — exec escalation + immediate mitigations (traffic cap & model rollback option)

On Tue, Mar 30, 2027 at 9:12 AM hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — escalating this to ops and exec attention. Summary:
> - Impact: elevated 429/5xx from repeated client reconnects causing "livelock"...

Confirmed and actions taken so far:
- Implemented traffic steering: 20% to v2, 80% to v1 for MedScale routing (applied at the edge, will propagate in ~2 mins).
- Increased platform streaming keepalive to 45s for the affected pool (runtime flag toggled).
- Flushed KV caches tied to MedScale api-key (completed).
- Enabled 10x trace sampling for endpoint; forwarding traces to the incident channel.

Preliminary observations (10 mins in): 429 rate has dropped ~40% and session reconnect loops appear reduced for the sampled reqids. We will continue monitoring closely and will revert traffic if any regression.

Next: run an 1-hour stabilized observation window and report back with aggregated token-level latency and incident impact. If MedScale confirms user-facing recovery we can close incident and draft credit memo based on measured downtime.

— Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
